basic.title: Basic Turn
basic.description: Walk through the real opening entry, one hand action, and one wheel action.

steps.welcome: In Seven Hatreds, you win by expanding control, taking a capital, or reaching 3 prestige first. Each turn includes one hand action and one wheel action, and this chapter walks one full basic loop.
steps.openingEntry: Start with the action rail on the right. In live play, both the hand action and the wheel action enter from here, and the current player chooses the order.
steps.handResource: The cards at the bottom are your main resource. Event cards are played directly, armaments cost an extra discard to play, and this step shows the most common pattern: discarding cards to pay for an action.
steps.selectRegion: Click Pidao on the map first. There is a nearby troop that can be pardoned here, so the result shows up on the map immediately.
steps.pickAction: Now click Grant Pardon. This is a faction action that directly changes the board position.
steps.payCards: Grant Pardon costs 3 cards. Click any 3 cards in your hand, then click Confirm Action.
steps.actionResult: After it resolves, 1 enemy troop beside Pidao becomes a Ming troop. The cards you just discarded have already turned into board control.
steps.moraleLevel: The number on top of each troop block is both its level and its morale. Damage usually lowers that level first, and a troop is only destroyed when it drops to zero. Higher levels also roll stronger dice.
steps.wheelMove: After the hand action, this turn still has one wheel action left. Click Free Move 1 on the wheel now.
steps.finish: You have completed one basic turn: pay cards for a faction action, then finish one wheel action. The next lesson is what happens when these troops actually fight.

fieldBattle.title: Field Battle
fieldBattle.description: See one full field battle with casualty order, dice, and post-battle occupation.

steps.battleOverview: This chapter starts from a field battle that is already engaged. A field battle is about troop level, dice results, casualty order, and what you do after winning.
steps.battleTarget: The current battlefield is Chahar. Read the map and the pending panel first: both sides, committed troops, and the target are already shown here.
steps.casualtyPriority: You must choose casualty order first. Click Lowest Level First now so the weaker troops lose level first, then resolve the battle.
steps.battleResult: After resolution, read the dice summary and the outcome first. You can directly see both rolls, the damage dealt, and how many troops survived.
steps.occupyRegion: This field battle is won. Click Occupy This Region now and leave the surviving troops in Chahar.
steps.finish: That is the core loop of a field battle: compare troop level and dice, decide casualties, then resolve occupation or withdrawal.

diplomacy.title: Diplomacy And Hire
diplomacy.description: Enter one real wheel diplomacy/hire step and see map control plus mercenaries resolve together.

steps.overview: This chapter focuses on diplomacy and hiring. It is not only about flipping map markers; it also decides where you can station troops and which regions become your vassals.
steps.wheelEntry: The wheel has not moved yet. Click Free Move 1 first to advance into Diplomacy / Hire.
steps.chooseTarget: Now the game is in Diplomacy / Hire. Read the prompt first: this action starts from Shanhai Pass, handles a neighboring control marker, then settles the hired troops.
steps.placeFriendly: Click the neighboring target first, then click Place Friendly Marker. A friendly region gives you passage and stationing now, and it can be flipped into a vassal later.
steps.hireOnly: After the marker change, click End And Hire. That will place 2 level-2 mercenary troops directly in your source region.
steps.finish: You have now seen both halves of the system: diplomacy changes map control markers, and hiring adds troops to your controlled region.

siege.title: Siege And Occupation
siege.description: See why winning a city battle is not the same as immediately taking control.

steps.overview: This chapter starts from the post-battle decision after Shanhaiguan has been breached. After a city battle, you still decide whether to occupy, besiege, or withdraw.
steps.target: Look at Shanhaiguan first. It has been breached, but it is still controlled by Jin, so the post-battle choice decides the city's next state.
steps.result: The panel already shows the city battle result. Read the summary first: 2 attacking troops survived, and now you decide whether they enter the city or stay outside as a siege.
steps.besiegeChoice: Click Besiege This Region now. Besieging leaves the surviving troops outside the city and does not change control yet.
steps.finish: That is one key difference between city battles and field battles: even after winning, you may besiege first instead of taking control immediately.

season.title: Midyear And New Year
season.description: Understand midyear checks, new-year maintenance, and why the game rhythm changes when the year turns.

steps.overview: This chapter is about seasonal resolution. Seven Hatreds is not only about the immediate move; when the wheel reaches Midyear and New Year, taxes, character checks, fortification maintenance, and year rollover all matter.
steps.advanceMidyear: Click Advance 2 while giving one opponent 2 cards first. As soon as the wheel enters Midyear, taxes and character checks resolve immediately.
steps.midyearSummary: Now read the Midyear summary. It lists the tax result, defeat markers, and character checks in one place.
steps.advanceNewYear: After reading Midyear, click Free Move 1. As soon as the wheel enters New Year, fortification maintenance begins.
steps.newYearMaintenance: Start with the maintenance choice. Click Auto Maintain now and let the system pay for every fortification it can still keep.
steps.finish: After the year turns, you will see the New Year summary and the next year title. That is the basic rhythm of one year moving from Midyear into New Year.

selectedRegion.title: Selected region details
selectedRegion.purposeDiagnostic: Only used for sample guidance, magic-wand work, and chain boundary repair; it is excluded automatically from formal mask/graph exports.

selectedRegion.truthDiagnostic: Diagnostic sample. It can validate direction but cannot replace formal region truth.
selectedRegion.truthAuthoritative: Explicit truth. The main pipeline consumes this region result directly.
selectedRegion.truthBootstrap: Heuristic bootstrap. It still needs chain refinement or promotion into explicit truth.
